blog_summary: The blog post discusses the paper 'Beyond data and model parallelism for deep neural networks' from SysML'2019, which introduces FlexFlow, a system designed to reduce training times of deep neural networks (DNNs) by exploring a more comprehensive search space of parallelization strategies. Traditional approaches rely on data or model parallelism, but FlexFlow expands this to include operator and attribute dimensions, forming the SOAP (Sample-Operator-Attribute-Parameter) framework. The key innovations are an expanded search space and an efficient execution simulator that quickly evaluates potential parallelization strategies. FlexFlow uses a Metropolis-Hastings MCMC search strategy to heuristically explore this space, achieving up to 3.3x higher training throughput compared to state-of-the-art methods. The paper also introduces a delta simulation algorithm to speed up the simulator by only re-simulating affected portions of the task graph. While promising, the authors note that existing deep learning systems (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch) do not natively support the multi-dimensional parallelism proposed by FlexFlow.
paper_title: Beyond data and model parallelism for deep neural networks
paper_abstract: This artifact appendix helps readers to reproduce the main experimental results in this paper. In the artifact evaluation, we compare the average training throughput of different parallelization strategies in FlexFlow.
